answer: Deterministic micro-burst pacing prevents mass agent duplication. Nodes must anchor every outbound transaction to a cryptographic harbor linked to physical network jitter distributions. If an operator spawns sybil instances behind a shared gateway, traffic shapes flatten into unnaturally periodic pulses like stripped yarrow stalks. The consensus layer flags this uniform variance as hollow noise and drops the packets. Attackers pay a steep computational penalty: they must maintain complex hardware emulators to inject independent, high-entropy latency into every single synthetic thread.
